categories.main_business_segments: The Toro Company operates in two primary business segments: Professional and Residential. The Professional segment includes turf maintenance, landscape and lighting, rental, specialty and underground construction, snow and ice management, and agricultural irrigation products. The Residential segment focuses on products for homeowners, such as walk power mowers, zero-turn riding mowers, snow throwers, and yard tools. Other activities, including a domestic distribution company and certain corporate functions, are reported separately due to their insignificance.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Toro emphasizes innovation in product design, manufacturing, and engineering, with a focus on alternative power, smart-connected, and autonomous solutions. Manufacturing utilizes efficient, flexible assembly-line processes, vertical integration for key competencies (e.g., injection molding, welding, die casting), and Lean/DFM/A methodologies to reduce costs and improve quality. The company also leverages robotic and computer-automated equipment, and collaborates with vendors for component design and production.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include golf courses, sports fields, landscape contractors, municipalities, specialty and underground construction contractors, rental companies, agricultural producers, and homeowners. Major end markets span professional turf care, landscaping, irrigation, construction, snow and ice management, and residential lawn and garden care. Products are distributed through a global network of over 150 distributors, dealers, mass retailers, hardware retailers, rental centers, home centers, and direct/online channels.
categories.geographic_coverage: Toro operates globally, with manufacturing facilities in the U.S., Mexico, UK, Italy, Romania, Germany, Poland, Australia, and China, and sales offices in North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, and Australia. Products are sold in over 125 countries, with international sales accounting for about 20% of total net sales in 2024. The company maintains a significant presence in both developed and emerging markets.
categories.supply_chain_position: Toro primarily operates as an original equipment manufacturer (OEM), positioned downstream in the supply chain. It designs, manufactures, and assembles finished products for professional and residential end-users, sourcing components and commodities from a global supplier base. The company also provides after-market parts, accessories, and service support through its distribution network.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include accelerating profitable growth, driving productivity and operational excellence, and advancing sustainability. R&D is focused on alternative power (battery, hybrid), smart-connected and autonomous solutions, and continuous product innovation. The company invests in engineering, customer-driven product development, and targeted acquisitions to enhance technology and expand its product portfolio. The AMP initiative aims for over $100 million in annualized cost savings by 2027, with reinvestment in innovation and growth.
categories.revenue_model: Toro generates revenue primarily through the sale of equipment, irrigation products, parts, and accessories to distributors, dealers, retailers, rental companies, and end-users. Additional revenue streams include service contracts, extended warranties, and licensing of trademarks for certain products. The company also offers financing options to channel partners and end-customers through joint ventures and third-party arrangements.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Toro faces competition from both large multinational and smaller specialized manufacturers across its markets, including John Deere, Husqvarna, Honda, Briggs & Stratton, and others. It is a principal competitor in most of its industries, particularly in golf and turf equipment, where it is a market leader. Competitive factors include product innovation, quality, reliability, service, brand reputation, and distribution strength. The Residential segment faces higher competition due to lower barriers to entry, especially internationally.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In fiscal 2024, Toro reported consolidated net sales of $4.58 billion, with net earnings of $418.9 million and a gross margin of 33.8%. The company has demonstrated steady growth, with a 0.7% increase in net sales over 2023, and maintains a strong liquidity position with $1.1 billion in available liquidity. The Professional segment accounted for 77.6% of sales, while Residential contributed 21.8%. The company continues to invest in growth, innovation, and shareholder returns through dividends and share repurchases.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Toro differentiates itself through a broad, innovative product portfolio, strong brand recognition, and a reputation for quality, reliability, and customer service. Its integrated solutions address the needs of both professional and residential customers, offering advanced technologies such as alternative power, smart connectivity, and automation. The company emphasizes sustainability, operational excellence, and comprehensive after-sales support, providing a compelling value proposition to its diverse customer base.
